what_it_does: AMD's Zen 5 is a chip design for personal computers, servers, and embedded systems that aims for both speed and efficiency. The core idea is to run at very high clock speeds (5.7 GHz) while handling many different types of workloads with flexible floating-point math units that can switch between narrow (256-bit) and wide (512-bit) data paths depending on the task. The chip uses improved branch prediction (guessing which instruction to run next), better cache efficiency (reducing trips to slower memory), and more register storage (temporary memory for calculations).
